title: MCP adapter close must release daemon-side session bindings
description:
Register item 5, SECOND HALF — reopened by worker-40286572 during the register close-out after a runtime probe contradicted the triage verdict. The triage pass recorded item 5 as closed on BOTH halves. Half one is genuinely closed. Half two is not, and it produced no task, which is exactly how an item is silently retired.

WHAT THE ORIGINAL FINDING SAID: "the HTTP session registry grows unbounded, and close() never releases daemon-side bindings."

HALF ONE — CLOSED, verified, no work needed. Per-session eviction exists at packages/mcp/src/http/http-session.ts:222, inside closeDaemonSession, which calls registry.delete(mcpSessionId) and then port.closeSession(mcpSessionId). It is wired to production at http-server.ts:213 through the SDK's onsessionclosed callback. packages/mcp/src/http/http-server-lifecycle.test.ts:35 covers it and asserts the exact call order bind then close.

HALF TWO — STILL OPEN. The adapter's own close() at packages/mcp/src/http/http-server.ts:303-309 does this per entry: registry.delete(entry.sessionId), await entry.attachment.transport.close(), await entry.attachment.server.close(). It never calls options.sessionPort.closeSession(...). The registry is this adapter's IN-PROCESS map; releasing an entry from it is not the same act as telling the daemon to drop the session. bindDaemonSession at http-session.ts:203-211 creates the daemon-side binding with await port.bindSession(...), so every session opened through initialize leaves a daemon-side binding that adapter shutdown does not release.

WHY THE TRANSPORT DOES NOT COVER FOR IT. The obvious rebuttal is that transport.close() might fire onsessionclosed and reach closeDaemonSession that way. It does not. In @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.30.0, dist/esm/server/webStandardStreamableHttp.js, close() clears _streamMapping, _requestResponseMap and _resumableStreams and calls onclose — it never touches _onsessionclosed. The only caller of _onsessionclosed is handleDeleteRequest, an explicit client DELETE. Read those bytes before assuming otherwise.

RUNTIME PROOF, not inference. A temporary probe was appended to http-server-lifecycle.test.ts: build an adapter with a recording sessionPort, drive one initialize, then call adapter.close() with NO DELETE. Result:
  AssertionError: expected [ Array(1) ] to deeply equal [ ...(2) ]
    [ "bind:bd274e14-2cb8-4103-b0d6-d9f77ac1f363",
  -   "close:bd274e14-2cb8-4103-b0d6-d9f77ac1f363" ]
Only the bind was recorded. The probe was removed and the host file restored byte-identical, sha256 22d9cd0a0036c0e3fee2da0baf5c1c19755d115cb603be6df8599153d0e9da6f, 287 lines. No probe file remains.

WHY EXISTING COVERAGE MISSES IT. http-server-lifecycle.test.ts:35 is the only test that records a close: entry, and it issues a DELETE before adapter.close(). By the time close() runs there is nothing left to release, so the shutdown path is never exercised. Roughly a dozen other tests in that file end with await adapter.close() purely as teardown, asserting nothing about it.

SECOND DEFECT ON THE SAME LOOP, in scope because the fix rewrites these lines. The loop awaits transport.close() and server.close() with no containment. One throwing session aborts the whole loop, so every session after it keeps its transport, its server AND its daemon binding — a partial shutdown that reports as a completed one. Whatever release call is added must not inherit that shape.

ORDERING IS ALREADY DECIDED BY THE CODEBASE, do not re-litigate it. bindDaemonSession tells the port FIRST and registers only after it accepts, so a failed bind leaves nothing routable. closeDaemonSession removes the entry FIRST, documented at http-session.ts:214-215 as "the session stops being routable even if the daemon notification fails". Shutdown follows the close discipline: unroute, then notify.

Re-measure every line number before planning. Recorded at HEAD 192360e in a shared worktree.
definitionOfDone: The adapter's close() releases the daemon-side binding for every session it tears down: options.sessionPort.closeSession(id) is called once per registered session, in addition to the existing registry.delete plus transport.close plus server.close. Prefer routing through the existing closeDaemonSession helper over open-coding a second release path, so the two paths cannot drift.

A test drives one initialize and then adapter.close() with NO intervening DELETE, and asserts the recording port observed exactly [bind:<id>, close:<id>] in that order. This test MUST fail against current bytes before the fix - run it first and record the failure, because a test that passes before the change is measuring teardown rather than release.

Multi-session case: two or more sessions open at shutdown each get exactly one closeSession, with no duplicate release for a session that was already reaped by an earlier DELETE - a doubly-released session is a different defect, not a stricter fix.

One failing session cannot abort the teardown of the others. A test makes closeSession (or transport.close) throw for the FIRST of two sessions and asserts the second session still had its transport closed, its server closed and its binding released. The failure is surfaced with a stable reason code identifying which session failed, never swallowed and never silently converted into a successful shutdown - epic rail 4.
Fresh pnpm --filter @moe/mcp typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/mcp test exits 0, and the pre-existing DELETE-path assertion at http-server-lifecycle.test.ts:35 still passes unchanged.
taskRails: Do not weaken or reorder the DELETE path. closeDaemonSession removes the registry entry BEFORE notifying the daemon on purpose, documented at http-session.ts:214-215: the session must stop being routable even if the daemon notification fails. Shutdown adopts that same order; it does not invent a new one.

The new test must be proven to fail on current bytes before the fix lands. Adapter close() is already called as teardown in about a dozen tests in this file, so an assertion placed there can look like new coverage while asserting nothing. Record the red.

Do not swallow a per-session teardown failure to make the loop total. Rail-4 discipline: the loop continues over remaining sessions AND the failure is reported with a stable code. Trading a partial shutdown for a silent one is not a fix.

Target <=250 physical lines per production source; split before 400. packages/mcp/src/http/http-server.ts is already the largest file on this path - measure it with grep -c '' before adding to it, and split rather than exceed.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red, and task rail 2 makes this step load-bearing rather than ceremonial: about a dozen tests in http-server-lifecycle.test.ts already end with `await adapter.close()` as pure teardown, so an assertion added there can look like new coverage while asserting nothing. Each test below MUST be run and PROVEN RED against current bytes, with the failure text recorded, before any production line changes. TEST 1 (DoD 2): build an adapter with a recording sessionPort, drive exactly one initialize, then call adapter.close() with NO intervening DELETE, and assert the port observed exactly [`bind:<id>`, `close:<id>`] in that order. Today it records only the bind — that is the reproduction, and it is the whole task. TEST 2 (DoD 3): open two sessions, DELETE the first, then close the adapter; assert each session was released exactly ONCE — the DELETEd one by its DELETE and the other by shutdown — and that no session appears twice. A double release is a different defect, not a stricter fix. TEST 3 (DoD 4): with two sessions open, make the FIRST session's release throw, then assert the SECOND session still had its transport closed, its server closed and its binding released, and that close() surfaced a failure naming the first session rather than resolving quietly. Assert the observable daemon-side state, never merely that close() did not throw — a no-throw assertion stays green after someone deletes the fix, which is precisely how this defect survived triage.

Implement the contained shutdown sweep in a NEW packages/mcp/src/http/http-shutdown.ts plus its one-line LF `.js` bridge, rather than inline in http-server.ts. Reason, measured: http-server.ts is already 312 physical lines and is the largest file on this path; task rail 4 says measure before adding and split rather than exceed. A new focused module keeps http-server.ts flat (its close() becomes a delegation), leaves http-session.ts at 224, and puts the sweep beside a single owner. Export `closeAllDaemonSessions(registry, port, entries)` which, for EVERY entry and independently per entry: routes the daemon release through the existing closeDaemonSession helper — DoD 1 prefers that over open-coding a second release path so the two cannot drift — then closes the transport, then closes the server. CONTAINMENT is the point: a throw from any one of those three steps must not skip the other two for that session, and must not abort the loop for later sessions; collect failures instead of propagating the first. Note that registry.entries() already returns a copy (`[...sessions.values()]`, http-session.ts:94-95), so deleting during iteration is safe and is not the bug it resembles. Also publish a small CLOSED shutdown-failure vocabulary here — one stable code plus the failing session ids — and, when any session failed, throw one error carrying it after the sweep completes. Deliberately NOT reusing @moe/contracts' runtime error registry: that list is frozen and request-shaped, and a shutdown fault never renders into a client response, so a local closed code in the style this repo already uses for recovery-install and event-stream is the honest home. Never swallow a failure to make the loop look total — rail 3: the loop continues AND the failure is reported.

Wire it: in packages/mcp/src/http/http-server.ts replace the body of close() at :303-309 with a call to closeAllDaemonSessions, passing the registry, options.sessionPort and registry.entries(). The DELETE path at :212-213 (onsessionclosed -> closeDaemonSession) is untouched — task rail 1 forbids weakening or reordering it, and http-server-lifecycle.test.ts:35 must still pass unchanged, asserting the same bind-then-close order it asserts today. Re-measure http-server.ts with `grep -c ''` afterwards: it should SHRINK slightly, and it must not grow past its current 312. Then publish the shutdown code vocabulary from packages/mcp/src/index.ts so a host can discriminate a partial shutdown — an unexported code nobody can import is the same 'documented obligation with no caller' smell this task exists to punish. That publication will redden packages/mcp/src/mcp-root-surface.test.ts, which pins the published HTTP value list and asserts the root namespace shape; add the new runtime value to that list deliberately, the way its own comment describes, rather than loosening the assertion. Turn step 2's three tests green.

Mutation drills, since DoD 5 and the promotion note both demand the release be proven live rather than asserted. For each: sha256 first, edit with the Edit tool, confirm the anchor matched once, run only the named test, reverse the edit, confirm the sha256 is restored — never git checkout, which reverts to HEAD and would destroy uncommitted work in this shared worktree. D1: delete the closeDaemonSession call from the sweep, leaving registry.delete plus transport/server close — TEST 1 must go red on the missing `close:<id>`, which reproduces exactly the runtime probe that reopened this item. This is the drill that matters; if it does not redden, the test is measuring teardown rather than release. D2: propagate the first failure instead of collecting it — TEST 3 reddens because the second session keeps its transport, server and binding. D3: swallow failures and resolve successfully — TEST 3 reddens on the surfaced-code assertion, proving a partial shutdown cannot report as a complete one. D4: release twice for a session already reaped by DELETE — TEST 2 reddens on the exactly-once assertion. Read every failure message and confirm it names the assertion the drill targets.

Gate, review, commit. Run `pnpm --filter @moe/mcp typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/mcp test` fresh in the foreground and keep the verbatim tail; confirm the pre-existing DELETE-path assertion at http-server-lifecycle.test.ts:35 still passes UNCHANGED, and that the suite grew by exactly the three new tests. Subtract the step-1 baseline and confirm no new failing path intersects the owned paths, disclosing any foreign red verbatim. Re-measure every touched production file with `grep -c ''` against the 250 target and record the numbers, including that http-server.ts did not grow. Adversarial review: is the DELETE path byte-identical; can any session be released twice, or zero times; does one failing session still leave the others fully torn down; is the unroute-then-notify order preserved inside the sweep; and is the shutdown failure reported with its stable code rather than swallowed. Then `git add` the two new files first (a commit pathspec naming an untracked path commits nothing at all), confirm `git status --porcelain` stages no foreign entry — apps/**, packages/core/**, packages/contracts/** and .moe/** carry other agents' work right now — commit by explicit pathspec over the owned paths only, and verify with `git show --stat`.

Close the two open disputes in writing, because both were raised explicitly for the planner to settle and neither may be left contradicted. (1) ANSWER architect-2aea4111's register conflict on task-963cf1d125134c6193b7af0e53deeac3, adding a comment there with the measurement: possibility (a) is correct and this task is real. 'Daemon-side bindings' names the HttpSessionPort the DAEMON implements — bindSession/closeSession — not the adapter's in-process registry, nor the transport, nor the server. The triage measured the registry, transport and server (all genuinely closed) and did not measure the port, which is the one thing close() never touched; the runtime probe recorded only `bind:` and never `close:`. So register item 5 was closed on its first clause and silently dropped on its second, and the reconciliation should read 10 created + 0 declined + 1 already-closed rather than 9 + 0 + 2. State plainly that the triage reading was reasonable and incomplete rather than wrong-headed — a compound finding needs a verdict per clause, which is the durable lesson here. (2) RECORD THE HOST-LAYER DECISION raised by worker-40286572: apps/daemon/src/mcp-http/mcp-http-session-port.ts declares boundSessionIds() documented as existing so 'the host closes outstanding sessions on shutdown', with ZERO production callers — only its own two tests. This task deliberately does NOT touch it: the DoD, the rails and the verification command are all scoped to @moe/mcp, and deleting a documented accessor plus its tests in apps/daemon is a separable responsibility in a different package. But it must not be dropped, since a documented surface with no caller reads as a discharged obligation — exactly the failure mode that produced this task. Create a follow-up task owning apps/daemon/src/mcp-http/** that, once this adapter fix lands, either wires the sweep or removes boundSessionIds() and its two tests, with the gap measured symbol by symbol and this task recorded as its prerequisite.

comments.content:
CORRECTION AND EXPANSION FROM THE AUTHOR, posted before this task is planned. I wrote the description above, then kept measuring into the daemon layer during my own adversarial review. Two things changed: the defect surface is LARGER than I described, and its blast radius is SMALLER. Both matter for planning it correctly, and the description alone would mislead on the second.

WHAT I GOT LESS THAN PRECISE ABOUT. I wrote that "every session opened through initialize leaves a daemon-side binding that adapter shutdown does not release." The release call genuinely never happens — that part is proven by the runtime probe. But a reader can infer unbounded process-lifetime memory growth, and that inference is WRONG. Measured at apps/daemon/src/mcp-http/mcp-http-host.ts:126-137, the sessionPort is constructed INSIDE adapterOf(), one per adapter instance, and doStop() at :204-215 sets adapter = null. The port and its Map die with the adapter. Nothing accumulates across daemon restarts. Do not plan this as a memory-leak fix.

THE SECOND, LARGER HALF I MISSED — A DOCUMENTED OBLIGATION WITH NO IMPLEMENTATION. apps/daemon/src/mcp-http/mcp-http-session-port.ts:62-65 declares boundSessionIds() and documents its reason for existing verbatim: "Real production surface: the host closes outstanding sessions on shutdown and cannot do that without asking." It has ZERO production callers. grep -rn boundSessionIds over apps/ and packages/ excluding tests returns only its own interface declaration at :65 and its own implementation at :104. The only callers are mcp-http-session-port.test.ts:284 and :288. An accessor was built specifically to serve a shutdown sweep, the sweep was never wired, and the tests exercise the accessor directly so its disuse is invisible. The daemon's doStop() closes the listener then calls adapter.close(), and does nothing else.

SO THE REAL DEFECT IS A CONTRACT ONE, NOT A RESOURCE ONE, and it should be planned as such. HttpSessionPort pairs bindSession with closeSession. Today bindSession fires for every initialized session and closeSession fires only on an explicit client DELETE. Any implementation of that port whose close does something OBSERVABLE — writes a durable session record, emits an audit or revocation event, releases a daemon-held resource, decrements a counter — would silently never receive it for a session that was open at shutdown. The current implementation survives only because closeSession happens to be a pure in-process Map.delete (:107-111) on a Map that is about to be garbage anyway. That is luck in the implementation, not correctness in the seam, and the next implementation of the port does not inherit the luck.

WHAT THE PORT ACTUALLY HOLDS, since it bears on how a reviewer weighs this: bound is Map<string, Accepted> (:71), and Accepted carries principalRef and sessionRef copied from the authenticator's principal (:83-85). It is authorization state, not opaque routing bytes — the file calls it "in-process routing state, never durable identity", which is exactly right and is why this is not an identity-leak finding either.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PLANNER — TWO LAYERS, and please decide deliberately rather than fixing whichever one you open first:
- ADAPTER LAYER, packages/mcp/src/http/http-server.ts:303-309. close() must deliver closeSession per session. This is what DoD 1 through 4 above specify and it is where the seam is defined.
- HOST LAYER, apps/daemon/src/mcp-http/mcp-http-host.ts doStop(). Either wire the boundSessionIds() sweep the comment promises, or DELETE boundSessionIds() and its two tests. A documented production surface with no production caller is worse than an absent one: it reads as a discharged obligation. My recommendation is to fix the adapter layer, which makes the host sweep genuinely redundant, and then remove boundSessionIds() rather than leave a second path that can drift from the first — but that removal touches a foreign package's public interface, so it is the planner's call, not mine.

EVERYTHING IN THIS COMMENT IS READ-ONLY MEASUREMENT AT HEAD 192360e. I wrote no bytes to any of these files; the register shell that produced this task forbids production code. Re-measure every line number before planning — shared worktree.

This is a CONTRACT defect — bindSession fires and closeSession never does — and the current implementation survives only because closeSession happens to be a pure in-process Map.delete. The next implementation of that port does not inherit the luck.

No call to options.sessionPort.closeSession. Meanwhile bindDaemonSession (http-session.ts:203-211) calls `await port.bindSession(...)` for every initialized session, so bind fires and close never does for any session open at shutdown.

WHY THE TRANSPORT DOES NOT COVER FOR IT. @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.30.0 dist/esm/server/webStandardStreamableHttp.js close() clears _streamMapping, _requestResponseMap and _resumableStreams and calls onclose; it never touches _onsessionclosed. The only caller of _onsessionclosed is handleDeleteRequest — an explicit client DELETE. This is why the DELETE path is covered and the shutdown path is not.

WHY EXISTING COVERAGE MISSED IT. http-server-lifecycle.test.ts:35 is the only test that records a `close:` entry, and it issues a DELETE before adapter.close(), so by the time close() runs there is nothing left to release. About a dozen other tests in that file call adapter.close() purely as teardown and assert nothing about it — which is why task rail 2 demands the new tests be proven RED first.

ORDERING IS ALREADY DECIDED, do not re-litigate: closeDaemonSession (http-session.ts:212-223) removes the registry entry FIRST and then notifies the port, documented at :214-215 so a session stops being routable even if the daemon notification fails; bindDaemonSession does the reverse, port first and register only on acceptance. registry.entries() returns a copy (`[...sessions.values()]`, :94-95), so deleting during iteration is safe — it resembles a bug and is not one.

SECOND DEFECT ON THE SAME LOOP, in scope because the fix rewrites these lines: the awaits are uncontained, so one throwing session aborts the whole loop and every later session keeps its transport, its server AND its daemon binding — a partial shutdown that reports as a complete one.
